title: GRPO-VPS: Enhancing Group Relative Policy Optimization with Verifiable Process Supervision for Effective Reasoning
data_curation: Not a focus of this paper. Training uses the MATH training set (7,500 problems, Hendrycks et al.) for math reasoning and the WebInstruct dataset (Ma et al., 2025) for general-domain reasoning (covering Physics, Math, Business, Economics). Evaluation spans MATH test, AIME 2024, AMC23, and OlympiadBench for math, plus GPQA, MMLU-Pro, TheoremQA, and the WebInstruct test split for general reasoning. PRM800K is used only to validate the quality of the segment-wise progress signal against human step labels, not for training. No new data generation, filtering, or de-duplication pipeline is introduced.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. The method is a single-stage RL fine-tuning applied directly on top of existing base/instruction-tuned models (Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B/7B, Gemma-2-2B-it for math; Qwen3-1.7B for general reasoning). There is no SFT warmup, no multi-stage RL ordering, and no cross-stage data mixing; the contribution is purely within the GRPO RL stage, replacing trajectory-level advantage with a hybrid outcome-plus-process advantage.
method: GRPO-VPS augments GRPO with model-free, verifier-free process supervision to fix GRPO's indiscriminate credit assignment. (1) Adaptive Entropy-based Cutpoint Partition: tokens with entropy above a percentile threshold tau (e.g. 0.95) are selected as cutpoints, and the response is split into M segments each holding roughly the same number of cutpoints (n=4 is optimal); this places boundaries at high-uncertainty decision junctions. (2) Segment-wise progress: at each segment boundary the ground-truth answer y* is appended and the conditional probability C(z<=k)=pi_theta(y*|x,z<=k) is read in a single forward pass; the per-segment signal is Delta_Ck = C(z<=k) - C(z<=k-1) in [-1,1], quantifying how much each segment improves the model's belief in the correct answer. (3) Hybrid advantage: A_tilde_k = A_i + alpha*Delta_Ck, where A_i = r_i - mean(r) is the standard GRPO group-relative outcome advantage and alpha=1.2 (stable over [0.8,1.4]). The on-policy gradient fuses sparse outcome reward with dense process reward. No critic, PRM, or Monte Carlo rollouts are needed, so it stays lightweight and scalable like GRPO.
eval_metrics: Primary metrics are Pass@1 averaged over 4 runs (temperature 1.0, top-p 1.0, max 3072 tokens) and average response token length (AvgToken); Math-Verify checks answer equivalence. Math benchmarks: MATH, AIME 2024, AMC23, OlympiadBench. General benchmarks: GPQA, MMLU-Pro, TheoremQA, WebInstruct test. Progress-signal quality is measured by precision/recall/F1 against PRM800K human step labels (F1 > 0.75 across 0.5B-32B models, up to 0.803 for Qwen2.5-32B). Baselines include GRPO, DrGRPO, GSPO, S-GRPO, Eurus-2-7B-PRIME, and GRPO with Skywork-o1-prm. Training uses verl on 8xH800/H100, 8 rollouts/prompt, batch 512, lr 1e-6.
key_results: On Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B, GRPO-VPS improves overall Pass@1 by up to +2.6 points over GRPO while cutting reasoning length by 11.0-13.7%; on Qwen2.5-Math-7B it adds +1.1 point with up to 34.0% length reduction (e.g. AIME24 31.7% vs Eurus 15.0%). On general reasoning with Qwen3-1.7B, gains reach +1.8 on MMLU-Pro (54.4%) and +2.4 on TheoremQA (37.3%), with ~50% shorter generations than the base model.
evolution_note: GRPO-VPS extends the RLVR/GRPO line (DeepSeekMath, DAPO) by attacking GRPO's indiscriminate credit assignment without resorting to PRMs (PRM800K) or Monte-Carlo-rollout methods like S-GRPO and MRT, instead reading the model's own conditional answer probability as a free dense signal. Published at ICLR 2026, it reflects the maturing trend toward verifier-free, confidence-driven dense rewards as a scalable alternative to learned reward models, and motivates further work on belief-probing supervision for efficient long-chain reasoning.
